text: Mira Patel: sharing the latest console form mock — trying a low-contrast dot for required fields instead of the full asterisk. also updated the destructive action flow (typed-confirm optional, undo toast). link: https://figma.redwood/company/console-forms Jonathan Wu: looks cleaner. my worry is discoverability for new users. dots could be missed in dense tables. :thinking_face: Priya Desai: +1 on discoverability. can we pair the dot with a hover tooltip and an accessible label? e.g., • so screen readers announce it. Alex Morgan: quick + thought — if we hide the asterisk visually, make sure form field focus includes an inline helper: "Required" under label when focused. prevents keyboard users from missing it. Kevin Liu: accessibility nit: screen readers rely on aria-required on inputs, not visual markers. make sure we set aria-required="true" and aria-invalid when validation fails. role=alert for inline error messages so SRs read them on update. Mira Patel: good call. proposal: keep subtle dot on default, show explicit "Required" text on focus/hover, and ensure aria-required="true" on inputs. saves visual weight but keeps accessibility. thoughts? Jonathan Wu: sounds reasonable. one more: analytics — can we A/B the dot vs asterisk for new signups to see if support tickets go up? Priya Desai: on inline errors — I'm leaning toward contextual inline errors for single-field mistakes and a compact summary at the top for multi-field submit failures. examples: - single field invalid -> inline error only, focus goes to first invalid field - form-level failure (e.g., conflicting fields) -> show summary with links to anchors Alex Morgan: agree. Also prefer adding shallow UX: show inline error as soon as user moves off field (on blur) but only show summary after submit. reduces perceived form noise. Kevin Liu: Implementation detail: use aria-describedby linking inputs to the error ID. For summary links, use element.focus() with tabindex=-1 so screen readers jump correctly. also ensure we don't duplicate messages (both summary text and inline read the same content). Mira Patel: destructive action flow question — typed-confirm (type DELETE) vs checkbox + primary confirm. tradeoffs: typed-confirm is heavy but prevents accidents; checkbox + big danger CTA is lighter. proposals? Priya Desai: typed-confirm for workspace/project delete. checkbox for less risky batch deletes. Also show an undo toast for both so accidental clicks can be recovered. Jonathan Wu: agreed. typed-confirm should be reserved for irreversible ops. Also add clear copy: "Type the resource name to confirm" not just "Type DELETE" — contextual is safer. Alex Morgan: copy tweaks: for typed confirm use monospace input and small helper text: "This cannot be undone" (aria-live polite). For checkbox flow, add subtle confirmation modal with focus trap and a danger label. Kevin Liu: accessibility: if we use focus traps in modals, remember to restore focus to the triggering element after close, and ensure the modal is announced (aria-modal and role=dialog with accessible name). Mira Patel: copying action items: - dev: add aria-required & aria-describedby to inputs (Kevin) - design: add focus-state "Required" that appears on focus (Priya + me) - eng: instrument A/B for dot vs asterisk for new users (Jonathan + Alex) - PM: document typed-confirm criteria, and add undo toast policy (Mira to write draft) design-bot: reminder: weekly design review scheduled Thu 10am — add this thread to the agenda? :robot_face: Jonathan Wu: please add. I'll block 10-10:30. Mira Patel: will draft the policy and post updated mocks by EOD Thursday. thanks everyone for the quick takes. :thumbsup:
